In this article AMZN Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 1:29 01:29 Amazon misses on Q3 earnings and revenue Closing Bell: Overtime Amazon shares plunged more than 7% in extended trading Thursday after the company reported earnings and revenue for the third quarter that fell short of Wall Street's expectations. Here's how the company did, compared with estimates from analysts polled by LSEG: Earnings per share: $1.89 vs. $1.96 estimated Revenue: $201.94 billion vs. $202.31 billion estimated Wall Street was also looking at other key revenue numbers: Amazon Web Services: $45.98 billion vs. $45.29 billion, according to StreetAccount Advertising: $19.64 billion vs. $20.82 billion, according to StreetAccount The company held steady on its capital expenditure forecast for 2026, saying it continues to expect spending will reach $220 billion this year. Tech's hyperscalers have been on a blistering spending run to meet the surge in demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure, but signs have begun to emerge that the capex splurge is moderating. Earlier this week, Microsoft lowered its capex forecast for the year to $170 billion from $175 billion, while Alphabet maintained its guidance at $195 billion to $205 billion. CEO Andy Jassy said on a conference call with investors that the company expects to "spend meaningfully more in 2027," and that Amazon has a "clear line of sight to attractive financial returns." The aggressive AI spending has eaten into Amazon's cash flow. The company posted negative free cash flow for the second consecutive quarter, recording an outflow of $42.4 billion for the trailing twelve month period, an increase of 386% year over year. In the prior quarter, the company reported negative free cash flow of $7.6 billion. The company said the shortfall was primarily due to an increase in purchases of property and equipment as a result of AI investments. Capital expenditures reached $77.3 billion during the quarter, ticking up from $35.1 billion one year earlier, and coming in well above analysts' estimated $58.7 billion, according to FactSet. Amazon said it expects fourth-quarter revenue to be in the range of $240 billion and $247 billion. The midpoint of its guidance was below Wall Street's expectations of $244.5 billion, according to LSEG. The fourth quarter is typically one of Amazon's biggest by revenue, due to the peak holiday shopping season. Sales in Amazon's cloud segment soared 39% year over year to $45.98 billion. That topped the consensus forecast for $45.29 billion and growth of 38%, according to StreetAccount. Jassy told investors on the call that he expects AWS will be a $1 trillion revenue business in the next five to 10 years. Amazon is facing pressure from Wall Street to show that its AI investments are lifting its revenues. The company pointed to growing traction for Bedrock, its AI model marketplace, along with its Trainium and Graviton AI chips. Jassy said Amazon's chips business "continues to grow triple-digit percentages year over year." He added that the company plans to make its Trainium chips available externally "late in 2027," assigning a timeframe to comments Jassy made earlier this year suggesting such a move. Third-quarter net income came in at $20.69 billion, or $1.89 per share, vs. $21.19 billion, or $1.95 per share, a year ago. The company said the decrease was driven primarily by a $9.5 billion pre-tax gain from its investment in the AI startup Anthropic , which was recorded in the 2025 third quarter. While the AWS segment continues to hum along, results weren't as bright in Amazon's retail business, which remains its largest unit by revenue, or its advertising segment. Online sales gained 2% year over year to $68.47 billion, which fell short of analysts' projected $69.68 billion, according to StreetAccount. Advertising revenue rose 11% year over year to $19.64 billion. That missed StreetAccount consensus estimates of $20.82 billion. headlines.article_text: Reddit (RDDT) Q3 2026 earnings report Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Reddit plans to test requiring users to log in to access its platform, a sharp change for a site long known for letting people browse without an account. CEO Steve Huffman said declining Google search referrals are part of a broader shift in how the search product sends traffic to the rest of the internet. Reddit beat third-quarter earnings and revenue estimates, but its fourth-quarter sales forecast fell short of Wall Street expectations. In this article RDDT Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Steve Huffman, co-founder and CEO of Reddit, speaks during the WSJ Tech Live conference hosted by The Wall Street Journal at the Montage Laguna Beach in Laguna Beach, California, on Oct. 21, 2024. Frederic J. Brown | Afp | Getty Images Reddit plans to require all users to create official accounts to access the social media platform, marking a major departure for the site known as "the front page of the internet." The company revealed the change Thursday as part of its third-quarter earnings, in which it beat on the top and bottom lines, but provided weak fourth-quarter sales guidance. The company's shares dropped over 15% after its numbers were released. Here's how the company did compared with LSEG estimates: Earnings per share: $1.40 vs. $1.35 expected Revenue: $895 million vs. $878 million expected Reddit CEO Steve Huffman told CNBC in an interview that the company's shrinking search-referral traffic from Google played a major role in its planned efforts to require people to become "logged-in" users. A previous Google search update designed to surface "authentic" content from internet forums helped Reddit grow its user base over the past few years, but the search giant's continued push on AI overviews and related chatting features has negatively impacted referral traffic . "I think fundamentally that relationship between Google and the rest of the internet is evolving, and so for us, this means a continued focus on our core users that come to Reddit directly," Huffman said. Previous Google algorithm changes would "kind of come and go," Huffman said, but the company's AI efforts represent "a fundamental shift in how the Google product works, from being a traffic driver to whatever's going on now." Huffman didn't provide any specific timing on when Reddit plans for the platform registration change, saying only that implementing it through the site would involve a lot of complexity . The company will begin testing in the fourth quarter outside of the U.S. He said that Reddit is still determining what parts of the service logged-out users will be able to see, and will iron out the details as part of its upcoming testing. Reddit said that daily active uniques, or DAUq, rose 12% year-over-year to 130.3 million in the third quarter, trailing Wall Street estimates of 133.7 million. U.S.-specific DAUq dropped 2% year-over-year to 50.7 million, which was below analyst projections of 53.5 million. Read more CNBC tech news AI build-out hits snag as Google and Microsoft put off raising capex forecasts Alphabet earnings miss reflects first real sign that AI is taking a bite out of search As Waymo expands overseas, it remains a niche cash-burning business Hands-on with Apple’s first touchscreen laptop: Touch is totally optional Huffman said that "search referral traffic is down meaningfully in this quarter" and that the trend will continue in the fourth quarter. He said that Reddit is continuing its effort to make its platform "a daily habit" for users. "So that's where our focus is: growing those app users and logged-in users," Huffman said. Reddit, which derives the bulk of its overall sales from online advertising, is able to monetize logged-ln users better than logged-out users , because those registered users are more active and valuable to advertisers itching to deliver more targeted ads. "The vast majority of our revenue comes from our app users and logged-in users are direct traffic, and both of those are up Q. over Q. and so that's where our focus is," Huffman said. The company's third-quarter sales grew 53% year-over-year, marking an end to the eight-straight quarters of revenue growth eclipsing 60% that it reported in July as part of its second-quarter earnings. Reddit said that fourth-quarter sales will come in a range of $1 billion to $1.03 billion, which was below Wall Street estimates of $1.05 billion. "It's still a strong guide," Huffman said about its revenue guidance. "We are still growing at an industry leading rate, and that's despite the headwinds from search referrals." Reddit's third-quarter average revenue per user, or ARPU, came in at $6.87, which was higher than the $6.50 that analysts were expecting. The company's "other revenue" segment, which includes its data-licensing business, jumped 35% year-over-year to $48 million in the third quarter. Reddit's two biggest data-licensing partners are OpenAI and Google. Huffman said that Reddit remains "in negotiations" with Google over its data-licensing agreement, and said that it is "only going to do a deal that makes sense for Reddit," if it chooses to continue the partnership. "I think there's a lot of strategic considerations that goes into that," Huffman said. Huffman called the required registration plan a "big change" for himself, considering he "grew up on the open Internet." "Reddit is the last platform to provide basically unfettered logged-out access, and that's largely because of me, I've been holding that line," Huffman, a Reddit co-founder, said. "I think users will probably go through the same understanding that I have, which is that it's a sign of the times. It's an evolution of how these platforms work." Huffman later expanded on the significance of AI's impact on Reddit's user growth in an earnings call with analysts, and explained that the company plans to continue spending on marketing efforts intended to offset search-referral declines. "This is a consequential time for Reddit, and this period does remind me of about 11 years ago when I came back to the company," Huffman told analysts, referring to when he rejoined Reddit in 2015 following it's then-chief Ellen Pao stepping down. "We had a lot of conversations then about what is Reddit and what is Reddit for, and what is our place in this ecosystem. And we've been having those conversations at Reddit recently." "Reddit's mission is to create community and belonging for everyone in the world, and while there's overlap between Reddit and other players in the ecosystem, whether we're talking about social media or AI search, fundamentally, Reddit is communities and conversations," Huffman said. Sean Gallup | Getty Images Amazon's cloud-computing unit reported more rapid third-quarter growth than analysts had projected. Revenue came in at $45.98 billion, up 39% year over year and above the $45.29 billion consensus among analysts polled by StreetAccount, according to a statement . Growth in the second quarter came in at about 37% . "Our core compute and storage revenue grew at their fastest rates in several years," Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said on a conference call with analysts. The AWS growth rate was the highest since the fourth quarter of 2021. Amazon remains the top cloud by revenue, but growth has also sped up at rivals Alphabet and Microsoft. On Wednesday Alphabet said the Google Cloud business, which contains infrastructure and Google Workspace subscriptions, more than doubled in the third quarter. All the major clouds have been racing to build data centers that can accommodate high artificial intelligence demand. During the quarter, AWS announced plans to expand its portfolio of Nvidia graphics processing units that can handle AI workloads. AWS also acquired data analysis startup DuckLabs and signed deals with Meta and OpenAI, according to the statement. The AWS segment generated $17.77 billion in third-quarter operating income, up 55% and more than the $16.97 billion StreetAccount consensus. The unit now accounts for almost 23% of Amazon's revenue, a record. On Wednesday, Microsoft published its first earnings report that contained revenue from its Azure cloud in dollars. Azure is 72% the size of AWS, up from 58% two years ago. AWS came before Azure and the Google Cloud Platform, with its first services appearing in 2006. "With our continued pace of innovation, new core and AI functionality, enterprises wanting to run their core and AI workloads in AWS, and the amount of capacity that we're adding each year, we believe that AWS can grow north of 40% in each of 2027 and in 2028, and be a trillion-dollar revenue business in the next five to 10 years," Jassy said. Google has been pumping up its cloud revenue by making its tensor processing units for AI available outside its own facilities. Now Amazon will adopt the strategy with its Trainium chips for training models, starting in late 2027. "With Trainium demand so strong, customers continue encouraging us to make it available outside of AWS. We intend to do so late in 2027," Jassy said. headlines.summary: Intel has been a Wall Street darling this year due to its emergence as a player in AI, but the company is being weighed down by a struggling PC market.
headlines.article_text: Intel (INTC) Q3 earnings report 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Intel issued weaker-than-expected guidance for the fourth quarter, citing ongoing softness in the PC market. "We see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year," finance chief David Zinsner said in the earnings release. Intel shares have rocketed this year, but sold off in October as concerns emerge about the AI buildout. In this article INTC Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan speaks during a keynote presentation at Computex in Taipei on June 2, 2026. Cheng Yu-chen | AFP | Getty Images Intel shares plummeted in extended trading on Thursday after the chipmaker issued a weak fourth-quarter forecast, citing continued softness in the global PC market. Here's how the company did in the third quarter, compared with estimates from analysts polled by LSEG: Earnings per share : 52 cents adjusted vs. 40 cents expected Revenue : $16.51 billion vs. $16.5 billion expected Revenue climbed 21% from $13.7 billion a year earlier, the company said in a press release. However, revenue in Intel's client computing and physical AI group fell 5% from the same quarter a year ago to $8.1 billion, missing estimates, even as data center and AI revenue jumped 78% to $7.3 billion. Global PC shipments declined 4% in the second quarter from a year earlier due to soaring costs for memory and other components, according to Counterpoint Research . For the current quarter, Intel said it expects adjusted earnings per share of 25 cents on revenue between $15 billion and $16 billion. Analysts were expecting revenue of $17.1 billion and EPS of 43 cents, according to LSEG. "We see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year," Intel finance chief David Zinsner, said in the release. "We will continue making disciplined investments in capacity and working capital to increase supply and support future growth." Intel's forecast reflects the effects of an explosion at a fab in Israel that killed two workers and seriously injured a third earlier this month. Zinsner told Reuters that the incident will cost the company about $600 million in lost revenue over two quarters, and said the company plans to start ramping up production there by the end of the week. Intel's stock has been on an upward tear, up about 150% so far this year, although it's down roughly 23% in October over growing concern over the size of the artificial intelligence buildout. "We will remain disciplined as we invest, and we will not spend $1 of capital unless we have confidence in the health of our products and process technologies, and clear evidence of customer demand," Zinsner said on the call. Nvidia, which has become the world's most valuable company thanks to its dominance in GPUs, is scheduled to report results in mid-November. AMD reports next week. Known best for its industry-leading central processing units, or CPUs, Intel has been a beneficiary of the rise in agentic AI. While chatbots and large models rely heavily on graphics processors from Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices , agentic applications such as Meta 's Muse and OpenAI's Dots lean on CPUs to help orchestrate tasks and data from a computer operating in the cloud. "We now expect industry server CPU units to grow more than 30% in both 2026 and 2027," Zinsner said on the earnings call. "Despite near term headwinds affecting the broader PC industry, we continue to see robust demand for CPUs and more broadly, for all our computing platforms in the long term," CEO Lip-Bu Tan said in the press release. watch now VIDEO 3:55 03:55 Jeff Kilburg on Intel: Foundry business is the catalyst driving the stock higher The Exchange Intel's foundry business, meanwhile, has struggled to find its footing. Intel is the only U.S.-based manufacturer of advanced logic chips, and is now in high-volume production of its most advanced 18A chip out of its new fab in Arizona, providing an alternative to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. The Trump administration took a 10% stake in Intel last year after the company had fallen behind on its 7- and 10-nanometer technologies. Nvidia and Softbank also invested billions in Intel last year. Tan has taken a more cautious approach to foundry spending than his predecessor, Pat Gelsinger, who launched an ambitious revival of the company's foundry business. Last week, Intel said crews have installed the first structural truss at its huge Ohio chip fab that was originally expected to deliver chips in 2025. Its next fab in Arizona is expected to begin operations by the end of 2028. In September, reports surfaced that the world's leading maker of high-bandwidth memory, SK Hynix may team up with Intel in Ohio to lease some foundry space to make memory chips at the new site. Neither company would confirm any plans. Oracle disclosed an expanded deal with Intel this week, announcing at its annual AI conference that it would deploy the chipmaker's next-generation Xeon server processors, as well as the latest rack-scale systems from Nvidia and AMD, as it continues to add data center capacity. Intel completed a $23 billion equity offering in August. Tech giants have spent trillions of dollars in recent years to meet insatiable demand for AI and the infrastructure needed to support it. The electric vehicle maker also revised its 2026 guidance to mark expected improvements in its vehicle deliveries, pre-tax adjusted earnings and capital expenditures. Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe has said the company will reach profitability this year on a per-unit production basis with the R2, a smaller and less expensive sibling to its current luxury R1S SUV. In this article RIVN Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Signage outside Rivian's offices in Palo Alto, California, Dec. 10, 2025. Jason Henry | Bloomberg | Getty Images Rivian Automotive beat Wall Street's third-quarter earnings expectations as it ramped up production of its new R2 entry-level SUV that the company has promised investors will lead it to profitability. Here's how Rivian performed in the period ended Sept. 30, compared with average estimates compiled by LSEG: Loss per share: 48 cents adjusted vs. loss of 62 cents expected Revenue: $2.16 billion vs. $1.99 billion expected Shares of Rivian were up roughly 7% during afterhours trading Thursday, after hitting a new 52-week low of $11.38 earlier in the day. The stock closed at $11.45 a share, down 1.9% The electric vehicle maker also revised its 2026 guidance to mark expected improvements in its vehicle deliveries, pre-tax adjusted earnings and capital expenditures. The new guidance calls for a pre-tax adjusted loss of between $1.75 billion and $1.85 billion — a $100 million improvement at the midpoint from its prior guidance — vehicle deliveries of between 67,000 and 70,000 units, up from at least 65,000; and capital expenditures of between $1.4 billion and $1.5 billion, $300 million less at the midpoint. Rivian attributed the improvement in its pre-tax adjusted earnings guidance to better-than-expected revenue related to its sales of regulatory credits, an IEEPA tariff refund receivable in the third quarter and its expected increase in vehicle deliveries. The R2 — the first deliveries of which arrived to customers in June — has become Rivian's best-selling model and was responsible for "much of the gain quarter-over-quarter," the company said. Rivian delivered a record 19,248 units from July through September. The company does not disclose deliveries by vehicle. watch now VIDEO 15:37 15:37 Why the R2 could be Rivian's key to profitability Autos The EV maker remains unprofitable overall but continued to narrow its losses during the quarter. The company reported a net loss attributable to common stockholders of $913 million, compared with a loss of $1.17 billion during the third quarter of 2025. Rivian's gross profit, which is closely monitored by investors, was $176 million during the third quarter, up from $24 million a year earlier. Its adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization was a loss of $435 million, a $167 million improvement from the same period last year. The company reported that its software and services segment continues to grow, generating $605 million in revenue and a gross profit of $256 million, a 42% margin. That compares to its automotive operations, which recorded nearly $1.55 billion in revenue and a gross loss of $80 million. Also on Thursday, Rivian reiterated that it expects the R2, a smaller and less expensive sibling to its current luxury R1S SUV, to have a positive gross margin by the end of the year. CEO RJ Scaringe has said the company needs to scale beyond current R2 production plans of 160,000 units in order to achieve overall profitability. "That ramp-up is critical for us getting to positive gross margin on R2 and that ultimately will contribute to positive gross margin for the business," Scaringe told CNBC's Phil LeBeau during an interview Thursday. "We're going to see that through the end of the quarter and the unit economics will continue to grow … into Q1 of next year as well." headlines.article_text: Coinbase (COIN) earnings Q3 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu In this article COIN Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT This photograph taken on Jan. 21, 2026 shows signage of the Coinbase logo during the World Economic Forum (WEF) annual meeting in Davos. Ina Fassbender | AFP | Getty Images Coinbase Global earned third-quarter adjusted net income of $719 million , up 66% from $433 million a year ago, largely due to a recovery in the cryptocurrency market. Coinbase said it earned $2.51 a share in the latest quarter, although it wasn't immediately clear if that compared with the 6-cent-per-share profit that Wall Street analysts had estimated. Revenue of $1.20 billion trailed the $1.233 billion expected by analysts polled by LSEG. Net income at the San Francisco-based platform surged thanks to the value of its volatile cryptocurrency investment portfolio, which can swing wildly even when the composition of the underlying holdings are little changed. The third quarter value of Coinbase's crypto investment portfolio climbed due to a resurgence in the digital asset market. The price of bitcoin — often used as a gauge for all crypto assets — rose 39% in the three-month period ended Sept. 30 and the flagship cryptocurrency recently changed hands at roughly $80,809. Building beyond bitcoin In the third quarter, Coinbase deepened its push into non-crypto products and services, including artificial intelligence integrations for traders, tokenized real-world assets and prediction markets. In July, VP of product Max Branzburg told CNBC that Coinbase would debut an "everything exchange" spotlighting tokenized stocks and other real-world assets, derivatives trading, prediction markets and early-stage token sales. The trading platform also introduced Coinbase for Agents in early October, supporting users that want to use ChatGPT, Muse or other AI agents to manage their portfolios or research and trade various assets. Coinbase also expanded its prediction market offerings, making a wider range of event contracts available to users. In the third quarter, prediction markets revenue grew to more than $200 million on an annual basis, while the number of traders on those markets increased 60% compared with the second quarter. headlines.title: Starbucks sales miss expectations, but its U.S. turnaround is gaining steam
headlines.summary: Starbucks' U.S. stores topped Wall Street's comparable sales expectations but its international business fell short of estimates.
headlines.article_text: Starbucks (SBUX) Q4 2026 earnings Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Starbucks posted mixed quarterly results in the midst of its turnaround. Comparable sales for its U.S. stores topped expectations but the metric fell short of estimates in international markets. In this article SBUX Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol speaks during the Starbucks Investor Day event in New York City, U.S., Jan. 29, 2026. Brendan McDermid | Reuters Starbucks on Thursday reported mixed quarterly results as its international cafes underperformed expectations. However, its U.S. turnaround continues to take hold, as its home market topped expectations during the coffee giant's final quarter of fiscal 2026. "We enter fiscal 2027 with momentum, a clear set of priorities and higher ambitions for what Starbucks can become," CEO Brian Niccol said in a video shared on the company's website. Starbucks is ahead of schedule to meet the fiscal 2028 targets laid out at its investor day in January, he said on the company's earnings conference call. For fiscal 2027, Starbucks is projecting adjusted earnings per share in a range of $3.15 to $3.25, above Wall Street's expectations of earnings per share of $3.14. However, its anticipated revenue decline of 1% is weaker than expected; analysts were forecasting net sales growth of 1.4%. Starbucks is projecting North American same-store sales growth of 4% for the fiscal year. The company's earnings and revenue outlook includes an additional week and the effects of the shift in its China business to a joint venture business model. Starbucks is also projecting slight deflation in coffee prices and slowing net new North American cafe openings, which will both weigh on its full-year revenue, according to CFO Cathy Smith. Shares of Starbucks fell nearly 2% in extended trading. Here's what the company reported for the quarter ended Sept. 27 compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG: Earnings per share: 80 cents adjusted vs. 72 cents expected Revenue: $9.14 billion vs. $9.23 billion expected Starbucks reported fiscal fourth-quarter net income attributable to the company of $677.2 million, or 59 cents per share, up from $133.1 million, or 12 cents per share, a year earlier. Excluding restructuring and impairment costs and other items, the company reported earnings per share of 80 cents. Net revenue fell 4% to $9.14 billion, reflecting the joint venture deal in China. The company's global same-store sales increased 7.2%, fueled by growth in average ticket, and beating Wall Street estimates of 6%, according to StreetAccount. Transactions grew 1.8% in the quarter. Starbucks' U.S. cafes reported same-store sales growth of 7.7%, topping StreetAccount estimates of a 6.5% increase. Under Niccol's "Back to Starbucks" strategy, the company has focused on improving service, making its cafes more welcoming and sharpening its marketing. The changes have helped to win back customers. "Starbucks brand affinity is at near record levels as our menu innovation, marketing and merchandise continue to create moments that drive culture and bring people into our coffee houses," Niccol told analysts. The company said its North American rollout of its fall menu, which includes the iconic pumpkin spice latte, was the company's strongest ever autumn launch day. And matcha is now a $1 billion drink for Starbucks. Outside of North America, the company's international comparable sales ticked up 0.9%, as traffic declines offset an increase to average ticket. That growth fell short of analyst estimates of a 3.2% increase, according to StreetAccount. After its China business transitioned to a joint venture, Starbucks has shifted most of its international business to a licensed model, allowing local operators to take charge. The company is also exploring selling a majority stake in its Japan business, Reuters reported in September. Starbucks opened 303 net new cafes during the quarter. In September, the company announced it would close about 1% of its North American footprint, or about 250 locations, as part of its turnaround. By the end of its fiscal year, across the U.S. and Canada, the company also completed more than 1,700 cafe uplifts, meant to make its stores more welcoming to customers. The company has said locations that receive a makeover, with tweaks like increased seating and softer lighting, see higher transactions in the aftermath. headlines.article_text: Stocks making the biggest moves after hours: AMZN, INTC, TWLO, RDDT Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Here are some of the companies making headlines in extended trading. Amazon — Shares slid more than 6% after third-quarter results missed on the top and bottom lines. Amazon earned $1.89 per share on revenue of $201.94 billion, while analysts polled by LSEG sought $1.96 per share on $202.31 billion. The company reaffirmed its full-year guidance for capital expenditures at $220 billion. Intel — The chipmaker tanked about 17% after guidance for the current quarter came in weaker than expected. Intel sees adjusted earnings of 25 cents per share on revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion. Analysts were looking for EPS of 43 cents and $17.1 billion in revenue, per LSEG. Sandisk — The data storage device manufacturer fell 2% even after reporting an earnings and revenue beat in its fiscal first-quarter financial report. It delivered adjusted earnings of $49.51 per share compared to analysts' estimates for $46.22, per LSEG. Sandisk also announced an eight-for-one forward stock split. Starbucks — Shares were off 2% after the company reported mixed results in the fourth quarter. The company delivered revenue of $9.14 billion, compared with the $9.23 billion estimate from analysts polled by LSEG, but also posted adjusted earnings that beat expectations. Growth in the company's international business disappointed, but its domestic locations topped estimates for same-store sales growth. Pinterest – Shares dropped 12% after the company's latest quarterly results missed expectations on the top and bottom lines. For the third quarter, Pinterest earned 46 cents per share on revenue of $1.17 billion. Analysts surveyed by LSEG, however, anticipated earnings of 48 cents per share and $1.21 billion in revenue. Fourth-quarter revenue projections of $1.425 billion to $1.475 billion missed the FactSet consensus estimate of $1.52 billion. Rivian Automotive — Rivian shares added 4% after the electric-vehicle maker beat Wall Street's third-quarter expectations as it ramped up production of its new entry-level R2 SUV. Rivian reported 19,248 vehicle deliveries from July through September, up from a year earlier. The company also revised its 2026 guidance, citing expected improvements in vehicle deliveries, adjusted pretax earnings and capital expenditures. Reddit — The social media forum tanked 16% after current-quarter guidance disappointed the Street. Reddit sees fourth-quarter sales in a range of $1 billion to $1.03 billion, while the LSEG consensus estimate sought $1.05 billion. The weak outlook overshadowed top- and bottom-line beats in the third quarter. Roblox — Shares of the gaming platform shed 17% after the company gave disappointing guidance for the fourth quarter. Projected bookings for the period range from $1.89 billion to $2.00 billion, while analysts anticipated $2.00 billion. The company also guided for adjusted EBITDA losses in a range of $70 million to $10 million. Twilio — The consumer engagement platform fell 18% after the lower end of its earnings forecast fell short of estimates. Twilio sees fourth-quarter adjusted earnings of $1.48 to $1.53 per share, while analysts surveyed by LSEG expected $1.49 per share. Stryker — The maker of medical equipment slid 12% on the back of a guidance cut for the full year. The company expects adjusted earnings in a range of $14.80 to $14.90 per share, missing the FactSet consensus estimate of $14.95. Organic revenue is expected to grow at a rate of 6.5% to 7% year over year, missing analysts' forecast for an 8.2% increase. CNBC's Davis Giangiulio, Sean Conlon and Deena Zaidi contributed reporting.
